title: Residential fires in 2025 and fire safety in high-rise and older housing estates
asked: Mr Ng Chee Meng asked how many residential unit fires there were in 2025 compared with 2024, and whether the Ministry will step up education, enforcement and inspections, especially in older housing estates. Mr Alex Yam asked, in light of the Tai Po fire in Hong Kong, whether Singapore's building, fire and construction safety codes will be reviewed for high-density developments and what further compliance and enforcement measures are being taken.
asked_by: Mr Ng Chee Meng and Mr Alex Yam
response: In 2025 there were 1,051 residential building fires, up from 968 in 2024, although fires as a share of total dwelling stock fell from 0.067% in 2021 to 0.065% in 2025. The Government has started reviewing early observations from Hong Kong's ongoing investigations and will announce the outcome of that review in due course. The Minister set out existing safeguards — the Fire Code, Town Council and MCST responsibility for common areas, SCDF aerial appliances reaching 90 metres, and refuge floors in buildings above 40 storeys — alongside community programmes such as Community Resilience Days and the Responders Plus Programme.

key_points.point: 1,051 residential building fires in 2025, up from 968 in 2024, described as a slight increase within a stable five-year trend.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: In 2025, there were 1,051 residential building fires. This is up from 968 in 2024.

key_points.point: Fires as a share of total dwelling stock fell from 0.067% in 2021 to 0.065% in 2025.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: The percentage of fires vis-à-vis our total dwelling stock has actually decreased, from 0.067% in 2021 to 0.065% in 2025.

key_points.point: A review of early observations from Hong Kong's investigations is under way, with the outcome to be announced later.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: the outcome of this ongoing review will be announced in due course

key_points.point: All buildings must be designed and built to the prevailing Fire Code.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: All buildings in Singapore are designed and built in accordance with the prevailing Fire Code

key_points.point: Town Councils and MCSTs manage common areas in HDB estates and strata-titled developments, including SCDF fire safety compliance.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Town Councils and Management Corporation Strata Titles (MCSTs) are responsible for managing the common areas

key_points.point: SCDF has aerial appliances reaching up to 90 metres and surveillance drones for high-rise operations.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: the SCDF has capabilities, such as aerial appliances, that can reach up to 90 metres, as well as surveillance drones

key_points.point: High-rise residential buildings above 40 storeys need at least one refuge floor per 20 storeys.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: high-rise residential buildings that exceed 40 storeys in height require at least one refuge floor per 20 storeys

key_points.point: SCDF responds to most fire and rescue incidents, including high-rise fires, within eight minutes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: The SCDF is able to respond to most fire and rescue incidents within eight minutes

key_points.point: Structures above 24 metres (about eight storeys) must have fire lifts switchable to manual operation; additional fire lifts are required at 40 storeys and above.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: all high-rise structures above 24 metres, or about eight storeys, are required to have fire lifts

key_points.point: Construction hoarding must be non-combustible, fire safety systems must stay functional, and bamboo scaffolding is not allowed.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: The use of bamboo as scaffolding is not allowed in Singapore.

key_points.point: SCDF runs about 16 Community Resilience Days a year, and more than 60,000 people joined the Responders Plus Programme between January 2024 and August 2025.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: from January 2024 to August 2025, we have had more than 60,000 individuals participating in the Responders Plus Programme

key_points.point: Home Fire Alarm Devices are encouraged for seniors and subsidised under the Enhancement for Active Seniors Programme.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: We have encouraged HFADs to be installed in the homes of our seniors. This is subsidised under the Enhancement for Active Seniors Programme.

key_points.point: Unattended cooking is cited as the main primary cause of fires.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Statistics show that the main primary cause of fires is actually unattended cooking.

left_open: Whether inspection frequency will be increased specifically in older housing estates
Whether fire drills will be introduced in public housing estates
How SCDF coordinates access to very high floors when lifts have broken down
Whether SCDF will work with the Ministry of Defence on aerial rescue measures such as Heli Safe
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered evacuation preparedness for elderly and high-rise residents, and SCDF response times and operational limits at height.
